## A principled Bayesian meta-analysis workflow

This workflow takes you from a review question to a reported result. Each stage lists the Bayes-Metaverse package(s) to use, the key functions, and related software.

The stages are listed in order, but the workflow is iterative. If diagnostics or checks fail, go back and revise the model.

```{r}
library(bayesmetaverse)  # attaches bayesmaDatR, inspectR, robbR, bayesma, bayesfoRest
```

::: {.bmv-phase}
Plan
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><span class="bmv-nohex">protocol</span></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 0 · Review question and protocol

Define the PICO, effect measure, likelihood and primary model. Pre-specify the priors and sensitivity analyses.

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/">PROSPERO</a> · <a href="https://osf.io/">OSF</a></p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-phase}
Prepare
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesmaDatR.png" alt="bayesmaDatR"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 1 · Data preparation

Extract and enter study data in a structured way, with one row per study (binary, continuous or count outcomes).

```{r}
bayesmaDatR::launch_data_entry()
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/inspectR.png" alt="inspectR"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 2 · Trustworthiness assessment

Assess each study against the four INSPECT-SR domains. Document the judgements, and decide how to handle studies of concern. This complements risk-of-bias assessment; it does not replace it.

```{r}
tw <- inspectR::inspect_sr(dat)
inspectR::inspect_sr_table(tw)
inspectR::inspect_sr_plot(tw)
dat_tw <- inspectR::filter_trustworthy(dat, tw)
```

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://lhdjung.github.io/scrutiny/">scrutiny</a> (GRIM, GRIMMER, DEBIT checks)</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/robbR.png" alt="robbR"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 3 · Risk of bias assessment

Visualise domain-level risk-of-bias judgements with traffic-light and summary plots.

```{r}
robbR::rob_plot(rob_dat)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 4 · Preliminary exploration

Explore the dependence structure, possible moderators and the distribution of effect sizes before modelling (PRIMED).

```{r}
bayesma::primed(dat)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-phase}
Model
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 5 · Model specification

Choose the likelihood, the random-effects distribution, the priors on μ and τ, and whether the model is one-stage or two-stage. Check the priors with prior predictive checks.

```{r}
fit_prior <- bayesma::bayesma(dat, sample_prior = TRUE)
bayesma::pp_check(fit_prior)
```

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://paul-buerkner.github.io/brms/">brms</a></p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 6 · Model fitting

Fit the model with Stan's MCMC sampler (by default, 4 chains).

```{r}
fit <- bayesma::bayesma(dat, stage = "one_stage")
```

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://mc-stan.org/">Stan</a> · <a href="https://paul-buerkner.github.io/brms/">brms</a> · <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/package=bayesmeta">bayesmeta</a> · <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/package=MetaStan">MetaStan</a></p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 7 · Model diagnostics

Check convergence (R̂, ESS, trace plots) and model fit (posterior predictive checks). If the checks fail, return to stage 5.

```{r}
bayesma::diagnostics(fit)
bayesma::pp_check(fit)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 8 · Model comparison

Compare candidate models using LOO or leave-one-study-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV), ELPD, CRPS and calibration.

```{r}
cmp <- bayesma::compare_models(fit, fit_alt)
bayesma::compare_table(cmp)
bayesma::compare_plot(cmp)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-phase}
Check
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 9 · Small-study effects and publication bias

Use funnel plots, Egger-type tests, selection models, PET-PEESE and robust Bayesian model averaging (RoBMA).

```{r}
bayesma::funnel_plot(fit)
bayesma::egger(fit)
bayesma::robma(dat)
```

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/package=RoBMA">RoBMA</a></p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"><img src="figures/bayesfoRest.png" alt="bayesfoRest"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 10 · Heterogeneity

Look at the posterior for τ and the predictive distribution for a new study. Consider robust or mixture random-effects distributions.

```{r}
fit_mix <- bayesma::bayesma(dat, re_dist = "mixture")
bayesfoRest::forest(fit)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"><img src="figures/bayesfoRest.png" alt="bayesfoRest"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 11 · Subgroups and meta-regression

Model categorical and continuous moderators.

```{r}
mr <- bayesma::meta_reg(dat, moderator = ~ dose)
bayesma::metareg_mod_plot(mr)
bayesfoRest::forest(fit, subgroup = TRUE)
```

<p class="bmv-ext">Related: <a href="https://paul-buerkner.github.io/brms/">brms</a></p>
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"><img src="figures/bayesfoRest.png" alt="bayesfoRest"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 12 · Sensitivity analysis

Vary the priors, the studies included (for example, excluding high risk-of-bias or untrustworthy studies), the random-effects distribution, and one-stage versus two-stage models.

```{r}
bayesma::sensitivity_plot(fit)
```
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><span class="bmv-nohex">in<br>development</span></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 13 · Sequential evidence

Assess the accumulating evidence with a Bayesian sequential approach (Spence, Steinsaltz & Fanshawe, 2016). The package is in development.
</div>
:::

::: {.bmv-phase}
Report
:::

::: {.bmv-stage}
<div class="bmv-hexes"><img src="figures/bayesma.png" alt="bayesma"><img src="figures/bayesfoRest.png" alt="bayesfoRest"><img src="figures/robbR.png" alt="robbR"></div>
<div class="bmv-body">

### 14 · Interpretation and reporting

Report the pooled effect with its 95% credible interval, P(direction), Bayes factors where relevant, the forest plot, MCMC diagnostics and the sensitivity analyses.

```{r}
bayesma::interpret(fit)
bayesma::overall_plot(fit)
bayesfoRest::forest(fit)
```
</div>
:::

## Related software

Bayes-Metaverse is designed to sit alongside established tools. These are maintained independently by their authors.

- [**Stan**](https://mc-stan.org/): probabilistic programming language for Bayesian inference
- [**brms**](https://paul-buerkner.github.io/brms/): Bayesian multilevel models via Stan using formula syntax
- [**bayesmeta**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bayesmeta): fast semi-analytical Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis
- [**MetaStan**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=MetaStan): Bayesian meta-analysis via Stan
- [**RoBMA**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RoBMA): robust Bayesian meta-analysis via model averaging
- [**scrutiny**](https://lhdjung.github.io/scrutiny/): error detection in summary statistics
